# Instruments: General synths

A note's `pitch` uses the **MIDI pitch (60 = middle C)**. Latest list: `muser instruments --family synth`.

| instrument | Recommended range | Polyphony | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `synth.poly` | 36–96 | 16 | Initial sound of the polyphonic synth (fairly plain). For a specific sound use the poly.* presets |
| `synth.fm` | 24–96 | 16 | Default sound of the four-operator FM synth; electronic and metallic, can be used for bass |

## Adjustable parameters of `synth.poly`

Override the sound of the chosen instrument/preset; write only the items you want to change, the rest stay as they are. `muser instruments <name>` shows the preset's current values.

| Parameter | Range | Automation | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attack` | 0 – 20 s | ✓ | Volume attack time. 0.001-0.01 crisp; 0.1-0.5 soft; >1 slowly fades in (pad) |
| `decay` | 0 – 20 s | ✓ | Time for the volume to fall from the peak to sustain |
| `sustain` | 0 – 1 | ✓ | Volume level held while the key is down. 0 = attack only (pluck); 1 = full volume throughout (pad/organ) |
| `release` | 0 – 20 s | ✓ | Tail length after release. 0.05-0.2 tight; 0.5-2 with a tail; >3 a very long bed |
| `cutoff` | 20 – 20000 Hz | ✓ | Filter cutoff: lower is duller and darker, higher is brighter. Bass 200-1500; lead 1500-6000 |
| `resonance` | 0 – 1 | ✓ | Filter resonance: the peak at the cutoff. 0.2-0.4 adds character; 0.7+ screaming (acid) |
| `filter_env` | -8 – 8 oct | ✓ | How many octaves the filter envelope pushes the cutoff. Positive = brightens on attack then falls back (a 'wah'); 0 = no movement |
| `filter_attack` | 0 – 20 s | ✓ | Filter envelope attack time |
| `filter_decay` | 0 – 20 s | ✓ | Filter envelope decay time: shorter makes a snappier "wah" |
| `filter_sustain` | 0 – 1 | ✓ | Filter envelope sustain level |
| `filter_release` | 0 – 20 s | ✓ | Filter envelope release time |
| `glide` | 0 – 5 s | ✓ | Glide time; only works on mono/legato presets (slides between overlapping notes) |

Automation column: ✓ = notes already sounding follow immediately; next note = affects only notes that start afterward; — = cannot be automated. See [automation.md](../automation.md).

## Adjustable parameters of `synth.fm`

Override the sound of the chosen instrument/preset; write only the items you want to change, the rest stay as they are. `muser instruments <name>` shows the preset's current values.

| Parameter | Range | Automation | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attack` | 0 – 10 s | next note | Attack time of all operators (also changes how the sound evolves) |
| `release` | 0.001 – 100 s | next note | Release time of all operators |

Automation column: ✓ = notes already sounding follow immediately; next note = affects only notes that start afterward; — = cannot be automated. See [automation.md](../automation.md).

### Tuning examples

- FM sound with a longer tail

  ```json
  { "instrument": "synth.fm", "instrument_params": {"release": 1.2} }
  ```


## Tips and common mistakes

- `synth.poly` is the initial sound of the polyphonic synth and is fairly plain; for good-sounding sounds use the `poly.*` presets directly (see poly.md).
- `synth.fm` leans electronic with a metallic character, and suits electronic bass and bell-type sounds.
